simple_definition: A chip company that designs its chips and also makes, packages and tests them in its own factories.
technical_definition: Vertically integrated semiconductor firm performing design, wafer fabrication and assembly/packaging/test in-house.

simple_definition: A chip company that designs chips but pays other companies to manufacture them.
technical_definition: Semiconductor company that performs design and sells chips while outsourcing fabrication to foundries and ATP to OSATs.

simple_definition: A factory business that manufactures chips designed by other companies.
technical_definition: Wafer fabrication operator manufacturing ICs for third-party customers (fabless firms and IDMs); a 'pure-play' foundry does not sell its own-brand chips.

simple_definition: A contractor that cuts, packages and tests finished chips for chip companies.
technical_definition: Outsourced semiconductor assembly and test provider performing back-end ATP under contract to IDMs and fabless firms.

simple_definition: The last manufacturing step: separating chips from the wafer, putting each in a protective case with connections, and checking they work.
technical_definition: Back-end manufacturing: wafer dicing, die attach, interconnection (wire bond/flip chip), encapsulation, and electrical test.

simple_definition: The main factory step where circuits are printed and built up layer by layer on a thin silicon disc.
technical_definition: Front-end manufacturing: repeated deposition, lithography, etch, doping and planarisation steps that form integrated circuits on silicon wafers.

simple_definition: Software that engineers use to design and check chips.
technical_definition: Software tools for IC specification, logic synthesis, physical layout and verification.

simple_definition: Ready-made building blocks of chip designs that companies license instead of designing from scratch.
technical_definition: Reusable, licensable design blocks (processor cores, interfaces, memory controllers) incorporated into SoCs; typically monetised through licence fees plus per-chip royalties.

simple_definition: A glass stencil holding a chip's circuit pattern, used to print that pattern onto wafers.
technical_definition: High-precision quartz/glass plate bearing a circuit pattern through which lithography light is projected onto photoresist; custom to each design layer.

simple_definition: A photomask factory owned by a chipmaker for its own use, as opposed to an independent mask supplier.
technical_definition: In-house photomask operation of a semiconductor manufacturer; contrasted with merchant (independent) photomask suppliers.

simple_definition: A light-sensitive coating on the wafer that hardens or dissolves where light hits it, so the pattern can be etched.
technical_definition: Photosensitive polymer applied to wafers in lithography; patterned by exposure through a mask and development.

simple_definition: The most advanced chip-printing machine, using extremely short-wavelength light to print the smallest features; made by one company.
technical_definition: Extreme-ultraviolet (13.5nm) lithography; required for leading-edge nodes (7nm and below per SIA/BCG); ASML is the sole supplier.

simple_definition: The older, more common chip-printing technology that uses deep-ultraviolet laser light.
technical_definition: Deep-ultraviolet photolithography using excimer lasers (ArF, KrF) whose gas mixtures include neon.

simple_definition: The machines used to build and test chips in factories.
technical_definition: Capital equipment for wafer processing (lithography, deposition, etch, implant, CMP, process control), assembly/packaging and test.

simple_definition: A generation of manufacturing technology, labelled in nanometres; smaller numbers mean newer, denser chips.
technical_definition: Manufacturing technology generation (e.g. 7nm, 5nm); labels are no longer physical gate dimensions but denote relative density/performance.

simple_definition: A chip custom-designed for one specific customer or job, rather than a general-purpose chip.
technical_definition: Application-specific integrated circuit; often developed with design-service firms offering turnkey spec-to-production flows.

simple_definition: A company that takes a customer's chip idea and handles design, manufacturing, packaging and testing through to finished chips.
technical_definition: ASIC service model with entry points (spec-in, RTL-in, GDSII-in, KGD-in) through to delivered product, managing foundry and ATP on the customer's behalf.

simple_definition: Newer ways of packaging that place several chips side by side or stacked so they work together as one faster part.
technical_definition: Packaging approaches (2.5D, 3D stacking, fan-out, chiplets/heterogeneous integration) delivering higher I/O density and bandwidth; done by foundries/IDMs in-house or by OSATs.

simple_definition: The small circuit board inside a chip package that connects the chip to the main circuit board.
technical_definition: Packaging substrate (e.g. Ajinomoto Build-up Film, ABF) providing interconnect between die and PCB; a noted shortage item in 2021-2022.

simple_definition: A reseller officially appointed by a chipmaker to sell its chips.
technical_definition: Distributor franchised and qualified by an original component manufacturer (OCM); the OCM-sanctioned channel.

simple_definition: Traders who buy and resell chips outside the chipmaker's official channel; useful in shortages but a counterfeit risk.
technical_definition: Independent distributors, brokers and online component exchanges sourcing from diverse, non-OCM suppliers.

simple_definition: Contract factories that assemble chips and other parts into finished electronic boards and products.
technical_definition: Contract manufacturing of electronic assemblies/systems for OEMs; a downstream system-integration step.

simple_definition: The business of servicing, upgrading and supplying spare parts for machines already sold to chip factories.
technical_definition: Equipment vendors' post-sale revenue from service contracts, spares and field upgrades (ASML term; Applied Materials equivalent: Applied Global Services).

simple_definition: A step in the supply chain where one region or a few firms supply almost everything, so a disruption there hits everyone.
technical_definition: SIA/BCG definition: a value-chain step where one region accounts for more than 65% of global market share.

simple_definition: A special gas mixture (including neon) used to make the laser light in older chip-printing machines.
technical_definition: Rare-gas/halogen mixture powering excimer lasers in DUV lithography; neon is the main buffer gas.

simple_definition: A stack of memory chips packaged next to a processor to feed AI chips data very quickly.
technical_definition: Vertically stacked DRAM with through-silicon vias, co-packaged with logic; increases test intensity and advanced packaging demand.
